title: Temperature Sensor Comparison
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Four sensor families on one temperature axis, with four real jobs to choose between them. Range rules sensors out before any other specification gets a vote.

learningObjectives: Recommend a temperature sensor for a stated application.
Compare measurement range, sensitivity, linearity and cost against the requirements of a task.

keyQuestions: Which specification should you check first, and why that one?
Why is the most accurate sensor not the right answer for a battery pack?
The BME280 is rated to minus 40. Why is that a problem in Minnesota and not in Georgia?
commonMisconceptions: Choosing the most accurate sensor regardless of the job.
Assuming a sensor outside its range simply reads inaccurately.
Believing high sensitivity and good linearity come together.
assessmentOpportunities: Recommends a sensor for a stated job and defends it against at least two rejected alternatives.
Uses range as a disqualifier before considering cost or sensitivity.
Explains the tension between sensitivity and linearity.
